name: Muse Spark 1.3
tagline: Meta's efficiency-focused update to Muse Spark 1.2 — same 1M-token context and pricing, released September 2026 with measurably fewer tool calls and tokens on coding work.
seoTitle: Muse Spark 1.3 — Meta's Efficient Muse Spark Update
metaDescription: Muse Spark 1.3 is Meta's Sep 2, 2026 flagship update: a 1M-token multimodal reasoning model at $1.25/$4.25 per 1M tokens that used ~25% fewer tokens than 1.2.
overview: Muse Spark 1.3 is Meta's update to Muse Spark 1.2, released on September 2, 2026 and rolled out the same day in Muse Code and the Meta Model API. Meta describes it as an improvement across agentic and coding tasks, shaped by what the team learned from months of Muse Code and Meta Model API usage.

The headline change is efficiency rather than raw capability. In side-by-side comparisons by Meta engineers, Muse Spark 1.3 proved significantly faster and more efficient than Muse Spark 1.2, using about 20% fewer tool calls and about 25% fewer tokens. Meta says the model is less verbose, takes fewer turns where they are not needed, and has a cleaner overall coding style.

For agentic work, Meta trained the model across a diverse set of harnesses so behaviour generalizes between agent environments. Given an open-ended objective it uses tools to build its own context from messy and conflicting sources, corrects gaps in its plan, and tracks what it has learned. It is also trained to ask clarifying questions on ambiguous prompts, ask the user for help when stuck, and confirm before taking consequential actions.

Muse Spark 1.3 keeps the 1M-token context window and the standard Meta Model API price of $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens. Reasoning modes that were already available shipped on day one; Meta says max reasoning follows after additional safety testing. On safety, Meta reports stronger resistance to adversarial inputs and prompt injections, plus better calibration on which actions are irreversible.
strengths: Efficiency: about 20% fewer tool calls and about 25% fewer tokens than Muse Spark 1.2 in Meta's own engineer comparisons
Long-horizon agentic work: trained across many agent harnesses, builds its own context from conflicting sources, and self-corrects gaps in its plan
Collaborative behaviour: asks clarifying questions on ambiguous prompts and confirms before consequential actions
1M-token context window with native multimodal input (video, images and documents)
Unchanged pricing at $1.25/$4.25 per million tokens, plus a $0.10/$0.20 contributor tier
useCases: Reach for it in Muse Code for long-horizon software work where token spend on a single long thread is the real cost driver.
Reach for it for agent runs that must survive messy, conflicting inputs and multiple interleaved tasks in one thread.
Reach for it over Muse Spark 1.2 when the job is unchanged but the bill matters — same price per token, fewer tokens used.

pricing.note: Standard Meta Model API tier. A muse-spark-1.3-contributor tier costs $0.10 input / $0.002 cached / $0.20 output per 1M tokens in exchange for Meta using the data to improve its products.

faq.a: Meta released Muse Spark 1.3 on September 2, 2026, rolling it out the same day in Muse Code and the Meta Model API. Reasoning modes that were already available shipped immediately; Meta said max reasoning would follow shortly after additional safety testing was complete.

faq.q: How much does Muse Spark 1.3 cost?
faq.a: On the standard Meta Model API tier, Muse Spark 1.3 costs $1.25 per million input tokens, $0.15 per million cached input tokens, and $4.25 per million output tokens — the same rate as Muse Spark 1.2. A muse-spark-1.3-contributor tier costs $0.10 input, $0.002 cached and $0.20 output per million tokens.

faq.q: What is the context window of Muse Spark 1.3?
faq.a: Muse Spark 1.3 has a 1M-token context window, unchanged from Muse Spark 1.2 and Muse Spark 1.1. Meta's developer documentation describes it as natively multimodal, taking video, images and documents as input in addition to text.

faq.q: How does Muse Spark 1.3 compare to Muse Spark 1.2?
faq.a: In comparisons run by Meta engineers, Muse Spark 1.3 was significantly faster and more efficient than Muse Spark 1.2, using about 20% fewer tool calls and about 25% fewer tokens. Meta also reports less verbosity, fewer unnecessary turns, a cleaner coding style, and more reliable following of long-form instructions.

No. Muse Spark 1.3 is proprietary and closed-weight, available only through Muse Code and the Meta Model API. Meta says a Muse Spark open weights release is on its roadmap alongside bigger models, but has not named a date or said which model in the family would be published.

versionHistory.note: Efficiency and usability update — ~20% fewer tool calls and ~25% fewer tokens than 1.2, better multitasking in a single thread, and stronger prompt-injection resistance.
Coding-focused update behind Muse Code — improvements in code generation, debugging, codebase understanding, and long-horizon developer workflows.
Adds multi-agent orchestration, 1M-token context management, computer use; Meta Model API in public preview at $1.25/$4.25 per 1M tokens.
First model from Meta Superintelligence Labs — small, fast, natively multimodal reasoner that leads on health.
